tweaks.name: Normalize pagefile to system-managed
tweaks.description: Repair-oriented normalization: hands pagefile sizing back to Windows (AutomaticManagedPagefile=1) while journaling the exact pre-change registry state.
tweaks.objective: Restore the supported default pagefile posture on machines where a third-party optimizer or a manual edit left a fixed/undersized pagefile.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Set-NxSystemManagedPagefile writes only AutomaticManagedPagefile=1 under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Memory Management. The exact original state is captured first through the journal's registry capture: the AutomaticManagedPagefile descriptor (existence, kind, value) AND the full PagingFiles REG_MULTI_SZ (for example 'C:\pagefile.sys 2048 4096'). Win32_ComputerSystem.AutomaticManagedPagefile and Win32_PageFileSetting are read as reported context only - they are never used as the restore anchor because WMI summarizes and can lag. Honest limitation: once automatic management is on, Windows may rewrite PagingFiles itself; rollback therefore restores BOTH journaled values exactly (AutoManaged DWORD and the original PagingFiles string array), which reproduces the pre-change state. The layout that is actually in use changes at the next restart, which is stated in the result, not hidden. Never disables the pagefile (that is NX05-003, troubleshooting-only).
tweaks.defaultState: Vendor/OEM images are typically system-managed; tweaked machines may carry a fixed size or a pagefile on a non-system drive.
tweaks.proposedState: AutomaticManagedPagefile=1 with the original PagingFiles value journaled for exact restore; effective pagefile sizing decided by Windows after restart.

verify.procedure: Get-Nx05PagefileState re-reads AutomaticManagedPagefile (DWord=1) from the registry and journals Verified; Win32_ComputerSystem.AutomaticManagedPagefile is reported as context (a WMI read failure is logged as Uncertainty, never treated as success).

rollback.procedure: Invoke-Nx05Rollback -TweakId NX05-001 restores the exact journaled AutomaticManagedPagefile descriptor and the exact journaled PagingFiles MULTI_SZ (value deleted again if it never existed), only-if-ours; restart required for the restored layout to be in use.

originalState.method: Registry-exact capture: Capture-NxRegistryValue for AutomaticManagedPagefile and PagingFiles (kind/existed/value/keyExisted) plus read-only Win32_ComputerSystem.AutomaticManagedPagefile and Win32_PageFileSetting for context.

sideEffects: Windows may resize the pagefile after restart within its own policy.
A restart is required before the automatic layout is actually in use.

tweaks.name: Custom pagefile configuration
tweaks.description: Per-drive custom pagefile sizing with exact MB values, journaled as the exact original PagingFiles MULTI_SZ and AutomaticManagedPagefile DWORD.
tweaks.objective: Give owners deliberate control over pagefile placement and size on a named drive, without ever disabling the pagefile.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Set-NxCustomPagefile replaces or appends ONE entry in the PagingFiles REG_MULTI_SZ for the requested drive (format '<Drive>:\pagefile.sys <InitialMB> <MaximumMB>') and preserves every other drive's entry verbatim and in order. AutomaticManagedPagefile is set to 0 first, because a custom size is ignored while Windows manages the pagefile. Both values are captured exactly before mutation (the full PagingFiles array, not a summary) and both are restored exactly on rollback. Validation: drive must be an existing 'X:' root; sizes are whole MB with a 16 MB floor (the System Properties page-file dialog minimum), maximum >= initial, and 0/0 is refused because that means system-managed and belongs to NX05-001. Trade-off text (no performance claim): Microsoft's sizing guidance states that pagefile sizing depends on the crash-dump setting and the machine's peak system commit charge, so there is no universal value; the registry-declared 1024/8192 MB pair is a starting point that the owner must review against this machine's measured commit peak, and it is never emitted into presets. Restart required.
tweaks.defaultState: System-managed pagefile (AutomaticManagedPagefile=1) or an OEM-defined fixed size.
tweaks.proposedState: AutomaticManagedPagefile=0 and the named drive's PagingFiles entry carrying the requested initial/maximum MB; other drives' entries untouched.

verify.procedure: Get-Nx05PagefileState parses the live PagingFiles array and confirms the requested drive entry equals the requested MB pair while AutomaticManagedPagefile reads DWord:0; other entries are compared unchanged; the journal records Verified only on exact match.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-Nx05Rollback -TweakId NX05-002 rewrites the exact original PagingFiles MULTI_SZ and AutomaticManagedPagefile descriptor only-if-ours (live values must still equal the recorded modified state); restart re-applies the restored layout.

originalState.method: Capture-NxRegistryValue for PagingFiles (full MULTI_SZ) and AutomaticManagedPagefile before the first write; both descriptors journaled in one apply entry.

sideEffects: A pagefile whose maximum is below the peak commit demand can produce commit-limit failures; sizing is the owner's decision.
Kernel/complete crash dumps require a pagefile on the boot volume large enough for the dump type - NX05-009 and this entry interact.
Restart required for the new layout.

tweaks.name: Disable pagefile
tweaks.description: Troubleshooting-only removal of all paging files with an explicit commit-risk consent gate and full journaled restore of the exact pagefile configuration.
tweaks.objective: Provide a reversible, consent-gated off switch for the documented symptom class in which a specific workload must run with no paging file - never a general performance tweak.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: TROUBLESHOOTING and mechanically preset-excluded. Disable-NxPagefile requires -Approved plus -AcknowledgeCommitRisk; without the acknowledgement it throws before any capture, journal write or mutation. It sets AutomaticManagedPagefile=0 and writes PagingFiles as an empty REG_MULTI_SZ (no pagefile entries), after journaling BOTH exact original values (full MULTI_SZ plus DWORD descriptor). Documented risk, stated in the entry and in the function result: the system commit limit is the sum of RAM and all page files, so with no page files the commit limit is only slightly below installed RAM (Microsoft page-file guidance); processes can fail allocations at peak commit, and kernel/complete/automatic memory dumps cannot be written without a pagefile on the boot volume. The change is effective at the next restart; Win32_PageFileUsage keeps reporting the still-active file until then, which the result states instead of pretending the change is live. Rollback restores the journaled PagingFiles array and AutomaticManagedPagefile exactly (only-if-ours), so the previous pagefile configuration returns unchanged.
tweaks.defaultState: Windows default: one system-managed pagefile on the boot volume.
tweaks.proposedState: No paging-file entries and AutomaticManagedPagefile=0, with the exact prior configuration journaled; effective after restart.

verify.procedure: Get-Nx05PagefileState confirms AutomaticManagedPagefile is DWord:0 and that no non-empty PagingFiles entry remains; the result reports effectiveAt=NextRestart and keeps Win32_PageFileUsage as pre-restart context.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-Nx05Rollback -TweakId NX05-003 restores the exact journaled PagingFiles MULTI_SZ (or deletes the value if it never existed) and the exact AutomaticManagedPagefile descriptor, only-if-ours; restart re-creates the pagefile.

originalState.method: Exact registry capture of PagingFiles and AutomaticManagedPagefile before mutation, plus read-only Win32_PageFileUsage context (allocated/peak MB) for the report.

sideEffects: Commit limit drops to slightly below installed RAM; allocation failures are possible at peak commit (Microsoft page-file guidance).
Kernel, complete and automatic memory dumps cannot be produced without a pagefile on the boot volume (NX05-009 conflict).
Windows support statements assume a pagefile exists; this entry is troubleshooting-only and never preset.
Restart required; no commit already in use is reduced by the change.

tweaks.name: Memory compression configuration
tweaks.description: Enables or disables Windows memory compression through the documented MMAgent cmdlets, with a 16 GB+ RAM threshold gate and the full Get-MMAgent state journaled.
tweaks.objective: Offer the documented compression toggle only where the trade-off is acceptable, and restore the exact prior MMAgent state on rollback.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Set-NxMemoryCompression drives the documented MMAgent cmdlets (Disable-MMAgent -MemoryCompression / Enable-MMAgent -MemoryCompression). Original state is the FULL Get-MMAgent output captured as a property bag (MemoryCompression, PageCombining, ApplicationLaunchPrefetching, ApplicationPreLaunch, OperationAPI, MaxOperationAPIFiles) plus SysMain service status - aspect-for-aspect, because Disable-MMAgent's backing store is not a documented public registry contract and NEXTRIX therefore does not journal or write registry values for it. Hardware gate: the reference research (UltraOS) restricts compression disabling to 16 GB+ RAM and notes that on 8-16 GB systems it increases hard faults under memory pressure; the function refuses to disable below -MinimumRamGB (default 16) unless -AllowBelowThreshold is passed, and the throw text names the override. Service precondition: Disable/Enable-MMAgent fail with error 1058 when SysMain is not running (reference note from UltraOS/SynergyOS); NEXTRIX never starts or stops services (SysMain is NX11-009 territory), so the function reports the precondition as a clear failure instead of silently starting SysMain. Verification re-reads Get-MMAgent and compares MemoryCompression. Rollback re-applies the journaled original value with the same cmdlet.
tweaks.defaultState: Windows default on supported builds: memory compression enabled (Get-MMAgent MemoryCompression=True) with SysMain running.
tweaks.proposedState: Get-MMAgent MemoryCompression equals the chosen boolean; all other MMAgent aspects untouched; prior full state journaled.

verify.procedure: Get-MMAgent is re-read and MemoryCompression compared to the requested value; SysMain status and the before/after property bags are included in the result. Documentation states no restart requirement for the cmdlet, so verification is immediate rather than deferred.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-Nx05Rollback -TweakId NX05-004 compares live Get-MMAgent MemoryCompression to the recorded modified value (only-if-ours) and re-applies the journaled original with Enable-MMAgent/Disable-MMAgent -MemoryCompression.

originalState.method: Full Get-MMAgent output serialized as a property bag plus SysMain service status; journaled before the cmdlet runs. No undocumented registry value is written or relied on.

sideEffects: With compression disabled, more distinct physical pages must be held for the same working set; on 8-16 GB systems the reference research records increased hard faults under memory pressure.
Requires SysMain running; NEXTRIX will not start SysMain, so the change fails cleanly on machines where SysMain is disabled (NX11-009 owns that decision).
ADVANCED and preset-excluded: never applied automatically.

tweaks.name: Memory pressure & commit monitoring report
tweaks.description: Read-only snapshot of physical memory, commit charge versus commit limit, and pagefile allocation/usage.
tweaks.objective: Give the owner the numbers needed to decide whether a memory change is justified at all, before any mutation.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Get-NxMemoryPressureReport composes documented read-only sources: Win32_OperatingSystem (TotalVisibleMemorySize, FreePhysicalMemory, TotalVirtualMemorySize, FreeVirtualMemory), Win32_PageFileUsage (AllocatedBaseSize, CurrentUsage, PeakUsage per pagefile) and Win32_PageFileSetting (initial/maximum). Derived values are arithmetic only: commit limit = TotalVirtualMemorySize (Windows reports the commit limit here), commit charge = limit - free virtual memory, used percentages of physical and commit. Microsoft's page-file guidance defines the commit limit as physical memory plus all page files, which is exactly what the report explains next to the numbers. The report states no recommendation threshold and makes no performance claim; a counter that cannot be read produces an explicit Uncertainty entry instead of a guessed value (SynToolkit uncertainty pattern, r4). Writes nothing, journals nothing.
tweaks.proposedState: Machine-readable report object with per-source values and an uncertainty list.

verify.procedure: The returned object has readOnly=true and carries every value with its source class; absent values appear only in the uncertainty array. Nothing is written, so there is no configuration state to verify.

rollback.procedure: Not applicable - read-only, no journal entry, nothing to restore.

originalState.method: Not applicable - no mutation; the report itself is the state record.

sideEffects: A single instantaneous sample; peak values outside the sample window are not represented (Win32_PageFileUsage.PeakUsage is the per-file peak since the file was created).

tweaks.name: Standby memory diagnostic report
tweaks.description: Read-only standby/cached page-list report. Explicitly NOT a standby cleaner and never scheduled.
tweaks.objective: Make standby-list composition observable so the owner can judge claims about 'standby memory' with data instead of a cleaner.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Get-NxStandbyMemoryReport reads the memory page-list counters through the WMI PerfOS_Memory class (Standby Cache Core/Normal Priority/Reserve, Modified Page List, Free & Zero Page List, Cache Bytes, Pool Paged/Nonpaged, Available Bytes) and reports each value with its field name. Microsoft's 'Memory Performance Information' page documents exactly these page-list buckets and that 'Cached' is Cache Bytes plus modified and standby-cache bytes; RAMMap (Microsoft Sysinternals) documents the prioritized standby list as a diagnostic view. POLICY: NEXTRIX contains no standby-list purger, no EmptyStandbyList binary, no scheduled cleaner and no registry 'feature' that empties lists - emptying standby lists is a measurement technique that discards cached file data, not a tuning action, and continuous cleaners are a rejected pattern (directive; UltraOS bundles EmptyStandbyList as a benchmark tool, which NEXTRIX does not adopt as a tweak). A counter absent on this build is reported as Uncertainty, never as zero.
tweaks.proposedState: Machine-readable page-list report with an uncertainty list; zero mutations, zero scheduled work.

verify.procedure: The returned object has readOnly=true, cleanerPresent=false and one entry per page-list bucket that this build exposes; missing buckets are listed in uncertainty.

rollback.procedure: Not applicable - read-only, no journal entry, nothing to restore.

sideEffects: Instantaneous sample only; no history, no alerting, no automatic action.

tweaks.name: Large System Cache
tweaks.description: Sets the legacy LargeSystemCache value that biases the file-system cache size on the server side of the memory manager.
tweaks.objective: Expose a legacy-era file-cache bias as an opt-in, fully reversible ADVANCED setting - not as a general recommendation.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Registry route through the shared engine: HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Memory Management :: LargeSystemCache (REG_DWORD) = 1. The value's existence is documented (Win32_OperatingSystem.LargeSystemCache exposes the same underlying setting), but no current Microsoft documentation describes its behavior on Windows 11 client builds; the historical guidance is server/file-server oriented, and this is why the entry is E0 and ADVANCED rather than a default. Behavior is a bias of the system cache working-set target at the expense of process working sets: on a client with an interactive workload the trade-off is a larger cached-file footprint versus less memory available to applications, which is why P6 (low-end) is not offered and presets never include it. Journaling is the standard registry pipeline (exact original value, deleted on rollback if it never existed) and the change is effective after restart. NEXTRIX does not write any companion 'Memory Management' value here; the XREF to the NX17-012 curated legacy set is documentation-only (no duplicate target).
tweaks.defaultState: Windows 11 client default: LargeSystemCache absent or 0 (client balance); servers historically default to 1.
tweaks.proposedState: LargeSystemCache = DWord:1, effective after restart, with the exact prior value journaled.

verify.procedure: Test-NxConfigurationState reads LargeSystemCache back as DWord:1 (configuration verification only; no behavior or performance claim is made).

rollback.procedure: Standard journal rollback restores the exact original value (or deletes it when it never existed); restart required.

originalState.method: 10-step pipeline capture of LargeSystemCache (kind, value, existence, key existence) before mutation.

sideEffects: File-cache bias at the expense of process working sets; legacy behavior with no current Microsoft documentation for client builds (E0).
Restart required.
ADVANCED and preset-excluded.

tweaks.name: Clear pagefile at shutdown
tweaks.description: Enables the documented security policy that overwrites the pagefile at a clean shutdown.
tweaks.objective: Provide the documented security-motivated option with its shutdown-time cost stated, never as a performance tweak.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Registry route through the shared engine: HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Memory Management :: ClearPageFileAtShutdown (REG_DWORD) = 1, the backing value of the documented security policy 'Shutdown: Clear virtual memory pagefile'. Purpose is data-at-rest hygiene on machines that may be physically accessed (the policy prevents leftover process memory in pagefile.sys); it is explicitly NOT a performance setting. Cost: every clean shutdown writes zeros over the pagefile, so shutdown time scales with pagefile size and disk write speed - the documented behavior is a slower shutdown, which the recommendation text states instead of implying any gain. No restart is needed for the policy to apply (it acts at the next shutdown), and dirty shutdowns/stops do not get the overwrite. Preset-excluded (TROUBLESHOOTING) because the cost is real and the benefit is security-specific.
tweaks.proposedState: ClearPageFileAtShutdown = DWord:1; pagefile is overwritten at the next clean shutdown.

verify.procedure: Test-NxConfigurationState reads ClearPageFileAtShutdown back as DWord:1; the policy's effect at shutdown is not something NEXTRIX can verify without shutting the machine down, which the entry states.

rollback.procedure: Standard journal rollback restores the exact original value (usually 0/absent); takes effect at the next shutdown.

originalState.method: 10-step pipeline capture of ClearPageFileAtShutdown before mutation.

sideEffects: Clean shutdown takes longer in proportion to pagefile size and disk write throughput (documented policy cost).
Does not cover unclean shutdowns or power loss.
TROUBLESHOOTING-only and preset-excluded: security-motivated, not a performance tweak.

tweaks.name: Crash dump configuration
tweaks.description: Selects a documented CrashControl dump type (small, kernel, automatic or complete) with the exact prior value journaled and the disk-space requirement stated.
tweaks.objective: Let the owner choose how much crash evidence the machine keeps, without ever turning crash dumps off.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Set-NxCrashDumpConfiguration writes only documented CrashControl values: CrashDumpEnabled REG_DWORD 0x3 = small memory dump, 0x2 = kernel memory dump, 0x7 = automatic memory dump, 0x1 = complete memory dump (Microsoft's memory-dump options page lists these exact values and notes that a restart is required). DELIBERATE POLICY: 'None' (0x0) is refused by the function's ValidateSet even though it is documented, because crash-dump destruction is a rejected recovery-sabotage pattern in NEXTRIX's REJECT register; the catalogue entry is about dump-type selection, not dump removal. Companion CrashControl values (AutoReboot, DumpFile, LogEvent, MinidumpDir, Overwrite, AlwaysKeepMemoryDump) are captured read-only and reported, never written - changing them alters behavior outside this entry's scope. Disk-space trade-off is documented, not estimated: a complete dump needs a boot-volume pagefile at least RAM + 257 MB, and the function warns (does not fail) when no boot-volume pagefile is configured, because the selected configuration is legitimate but could not produce the chosen dump. Restart required.
tweaks.defaultState: Windows 11 default: automatic memory dump (CrashDumpEnabled=7), %SystemRoot%\Memory.dmp, overwrite enabled.
tweaks.proposedState: CrashDumpEnabled equals the chosen documented dump type; every other CrashControl value unchanged; exact prior value journaled.

verify.procedure: Test-NxConfigurationState re-reads CrashDumpEnabled as the documented DWord for the chosen type; the result lists the read-only companion values and any boot-volume-pagefile warning. Restart is required before the new dump type is used.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-Nx05Rollback -TweakId NX05-009 checks that live CrashDumpEnabled still equals the recorded modified value, then restores the exact journaled original descriptor (or deletes it if it never existed).

originalState.method: Exact Capture-NxRegistryValue of CrashDumpEnabled plus read-only capture of the companion CrashControl values and of Win32_PageFileSetting for the boot-volume warning.

sideEffects: Complete dumps can occupy roughly RAM + 257 MB on the boot volume; kernel/automatic dumps are smaller but still sized by the dump configuration.
Requires a boot-volume pagefile for kernel, complete and automatic dumps; NX05-003 conflicts with this entry.
Restart required.
Dump collection itself is Windows behavior; NEXTRIX does not add a dump collector or uploader.

tweaks.name: Pool limit configuration
tweaks.description: Troubleshooting-only paged/nonpaged pool limit adjustment, gated on a documented symptom note and journaled exactly.
tweaks.objective: Give an owner a reversible route for a documented kernel-pool exhaustion symptom, with the E0 evidence limitation stated up front.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Set-NxPoolLimitConfiguration writes PoolUsageMaximum (decimal percent at which the memory manager starts trimming the paged pool; the Microsoft troubleshooting article documents 60 instead of the default 80) and, only when explicitly requested, PagedPoolSize / NonPagedPoolSize as byte values in the Memory Management key. Gate: the function requires -AcknowledgeSymptom AND a non-empty -SymptomNote, so it can only run against the documented symptom class (Event ID 2020/2004-style paged-pool exhaustion), and it refuses to run with no value selected. EVIDENCE HONESTY: the Microsoft article that documents these values is written for a 32-bit Windows Server 2003-era failure mode and itself warns that PagedPoolSize=0xFFFFFFFF can exhaust free system PTEs; there is no current documentation of a benefit on Windows 11 client builds - hence E0, TROUBLESHOOTING and preset-excluded. Each targeted value is captured exactly (existence/kind/value) and only the values actually changed are restored on rollback, so a divergence in one value never blocks restoring another. Restart required.
tweaks.defaultState: Windows default: no PoolUsageMaximum override (trim at the default 80% of PagedPoolMax) and pool size chosen by the memory manager.
tweaks.proposedState: The requested pool values exist with the requested data; every other Memory Management value untouched; prior descriptors journaled.

parameters.symptomNote: Documented paged-pool exhaustion symptom class (Event ID 2020/2004); see documentationSource

verify.procedure: Each targeted value is re-read with Test-NxConfigurationState and reported per value; the journal records Verified only when every changed value matches. The result restates that configuration verification is not proof the symptom is resolved (owner-verified).

rollback.procedure: Invoke-Nx05Rollback -TweakId NX05-010 restores each journaled original descriptor per value, only-if-ours per value (a value the user changed afterwards is reported diverged and left untouched).

originalState.method: Per-value exact capture (existence/kind/value) of PoolUsageMaximum, PagedPoolSize and NonPagedPoolSize before the first write; only values actually targeted are journaled as modified.

sideEffects: Kernel pool sizing is a global memory-manager parameter: a larger pool reduces memory available elsewhere, and PagedPoolSize=0xFFFFFFFF is explicitly cautioned in the Microsoft article.
TROUBLESHOOTING/E0 and preset-excluded: only against the documented symptom, never as a general tweak.
Restart required.

tweaks.name: Memory diagnostics suite
tweaks.description: One read-only call that returns MMAgent state, physical-RAM inventory, commit limit/charge, pagefile summary and the standby-list snapshot.
tweaks.objective: Provide the complete pre-decision evidence set for every NX05 mutation in a single, reproducible report.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Get-NxMemoryDiagnosticsReport composes NX05-005 (pressure/commit) and NX05-006 (page lists) with Get-MMAgent state, SysMain status, Win32_PhysicalMemory module inventory (capacity, speed, configured clock, SMBIOS memory type, form factor, bank label) and the pagefile summary including Win32_ComputerSystem.AutomaticManagedPagefile. Every section is read-only; failures degrade to explicit Uncertainty entries per section so a partial report is never mistaken for a complete one (SynToolkit uncertainty model, r4). The suite exists so that a recommendation for NX05-002/003/004/007/010 is grounded in this machine's numbers (RAM total, commit peak, pagefile allocation) rather than a generic rule, and so that the same report can be captured before and after a change without adding any instrumentation.
tweaks.proposedState: Machine-readable combined report object with per-section sources and an uncertainty list.

verify.procedure: The returned object has readOnly=true and separate sections for mmAgent, ramModules, commit, pagefiles, pressure and pageLists; a section that could not be read is present in uncertainty.

rollback.procedure: Not applicable - read-only, no journal entry, nothing to restore.

originalState.method: Not applicable - no mutation; the report is designed to serve as the before/after record.

sideEffects: Instantaneous sample; Get-MMAgent state may require elevation, in which case that section reports uncertainty instead of failing the whole suite.
